learn.title: Pumped Hydro Storage: The World's Largest Battery
learn.intro: Pumped hydro storage is the world's largest battery technology, accounting for over 90% of global energy storage capacity. It stores electricity by moving water between two reservoirs, helping grids balance variable renewable energy supply and demand reliably.
learn.c1_text: Pumped hydro uses two reservoirs at different elevations. During excess power, water is pumped uphill to the upper reservoir. When electricity is needed, water flows down through turbines, generating power like a conventional hydroelectric plant. It acts like a giant rechargeable battery.
learn.c2_text: Modern pumped hydro achieves 75–80% round-trip efficiency. A single facility like China's Fengning plant can store 40 GWh, enough to power hundreds of thousands of homes overnight. It responds within seconds, providing grid stability services beyond simple energy storage.
learn.c3_text: India is planning 96 GW of pumped storage capacity to support its 500 GW renewable target by 2030. The Tehri hydro complex in Uttarakhand and proposed projects in Andhra Pradesh demonstrate India's recognition that pumped hydro is essential for a reliable clean grid.
learn.stat1: Global pumped hydro capacity: ~160 GW installed worldwide
learn.stat2: Pumped hydro provides over 90% of global utility-scale energy storage
learn.stat3: China's Fengning plant stores 40 GWh — world's largest battery
learn.stat4: India targets 96 GW of new pumped hydro storage by 2030

learn.title: Carbon Markets and Credits
learn.intro: Carbon markets put a price on greenhouse gas emissions, creating financial incentives for clean energy deployment. By trading carbon credits, companies can offset emissions while funding renewable projects, accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels globally.
learn.c1_text: Under cap-and-trade, governments set a declining cap on total emissions. Companies receive or buy emission allowances. Those emitting less can sell unused credits to heavier polluters. The EU ETS covers around 40% of Europe's emissions and trades billions of euros monthly.
learn.c2_text: Carbon credits represent one tonne of CO2 avoided or removed. Voluntary markets fund projects like reforestation and renewable energy in developing nations. Verified credits ensure additionality, meaning reductions wouldn't have happened without the project financing.
learn.c3_text: India launched the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme in 2024, creating an Indian Carbon Market to incentivize decarbonization. The PAT scheme already covers over 1,000 industrial facilities. India's market aims to align with international frameworks while supporting domestic climate goals.
learn.stat1: EU ETS carbon price reached over €90 per tonne in 2024
learn.stat2: Global voluntary carbon market valued at ~$2 billion (2023)
learn.stat3: India's PAT scheme covers 1,000+ industrial facilities
learn.stat4: Carbon markets cover roughly 25% of global emissions

learn.title: How the Electricity Grid Balances Real Time
learn.intro: The electricity grid must balance supply and demand every second, since electricity cannot be stored easily. As renewables like solar and wind introduce variability, grid operators use sophisticated technologies and markets to maintain stable frequency and reliable power delivery.
learn.c1_text: Grids operate at fixed frequencies—60 Hz in North America, 50 Hz in India. Frequency deviations signal imbalance between supply and demand. Operators must match generation to consumption within seconds, like a cyclist maintaining balance while pedaling uphill or downhill constantly.
learn.c2_text: Modern grid operators use AI-powered forecasting to predict solar and wind output hours ahead. Automated dispatch systems adjust generator output every 4 seconds. Advanced inverters help renewables provide grid services like frequency regulation that traditionally required fossil fuel plants.
learn.c3_text: India operates one synchronized grid connecting all regions, enabling power transfer across 4,000+ km. The Green Energy Corridors project integrates renewable zones with demand centers. POSOCO (now Grid-Controller of India) manages real-time balancing for over 400 GW of capacity.
learn.stat1: Grid frequency must stay within ±0.05 Hz of target
learn.stat2: India operates one synchronized national grid (since 2013)
learn.stat3: Modern dispatch systems adjust output every 4 seconds
learn.stat4: India's peak electricity demand reached 240 GW in 2024

learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Earth's Heat
learn.intro: Geothermal energy harnesses Earth's internal heat to generate electricity and provide direct heating. Available 24/7 regardless of weather, it offers baseload renewable power with a tiny land footprint, complementing intermittent solar and wind resources.
learn.c1_text: Earth's core reaches 6,000°C, creating heat that rises toward the surface. Wells drilled 2–4 km deep access reservoirs of hot water and steam. Like a pressure cooker, this steam drives turbines to generate electricity, providing power that works day and night, unlike solar.
learn.c2_text: EGS technology fractures hot dry rock where natural reservoirs don't exist, expanding geothermal beyond volcanic regions. Water injected into these fractures returns as steam at 200–300°C. This breakthrough could unlock 100+ GW of geothermal capacity globally in the coming decades.
learn.c3_text: India has identified 10,000+ MW of geothermal potential across regions like Ladakh, Manipur, and Gujarat. Puga valley in Ladakh sits on a geothermal belt with surface temperatures reaching 140°C. Ongoing exploration aims to power remote Himalayan communities with reliable clean energy.
learn.stat1: Geothermal provides 24/7 baseload power at 90%+ capacity factor
learn.stat3: Iceland sources 66% of primary energy from geothermal

learn.title: Flow Batteries for Grid Scale Storage
learn.intro: Flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes contained in external tanks, enabling independent scaling of power and capacity. Vanadium and iron-based systems offer long-duration storage suited to grid applications, with decades-long lifespans surpassing lithium-ion batteries.
learn.c1_text: Unlike lithium batteries where energy sits inside cells, flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolyte tanks. The bigger the tanks, the more energy stored; the bigger the stack, the more power produced. Think of it as a fuel cell that can be electrically refilled instantly.
learn.c2_text: Vanadium redox batteries use the same element in both tanks, eliminating cross-contamination and enabling 20,000+ cycles. Iron-based systems use cheaper, abundant materials—essentially rust and salt—reducing costs by 50–70% but with shorter track records. Both avoid lithium supply chain concerns.
learn.c3_text: India's first commercial vanadium flow battery was deployed in Ladakh for high-altitude microgrids. The Custom Duty exemption on flow battery components and India's National Green Hydrogen Mission are driving pilot projects. Flow batteries suit India's hot climate where lithium batteries degrade faster.
learn.stat1: Vanadium flow batteries last 20,000+ charge cycles
learn.stat2: Iron flow battery costs ~$50/kWh vs lithium $130/kWh

learn.title: Agrivoltaics: Solar Meets Farming
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics combines solar panels with crops or grazing on the same land, doubling land productivity. This dual-use approach addresses food-energy-water tradeoffs, supports farmers with additional income, and accelerates renewable deployment without sacrificing agricultural output.
learn.c1_text: Elevated solar panels cast partial shade that protects crops like tomatoes, berries, and spices from intense heat. Studies show some crops yield 60% more under agrivoltaic systems due to reduced evaporation and heat stress. The land produces both food and clean electricity simultaneously.
learn.c2_text: Sheep grazing under solar panels provides free vegetation management, reducing maintenance costs by 30–50%. Native pollinator habitats beneath panels boost bee populations supporting nearby farms. This creates a three-way synergy: energy generation, agriculture, and biodiversity enhancement on shared land.
learn.c3_text: India's ICAR and state governments are piloting agrivoltaics in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Rajasthan. The PM-KUSUM scheme supports solar pumps that could integrate with agrivoltaic designs. India's high solar irradiance and small farm sizes make it ideal for growing crops like coriander and turmeric under elevated panels.
